rubric_items.reason: All eleven known REQs (REQ-1 to REQ-11) are traced by S-1, S-2 or S-3; there are no assumed REQs.
S-1 and S-2 each deliver one outcome. S-3 bundles four different constraints (link, no contact details, no medical history, page unchanged).

The ACs are Given/When/Then with concrete values and good partitions for the Inactive and closed-status cases. The REQ-11 unchanged check skips the Completed and No-show partitions, and the fee ACs do not test a fee of 1,000 rupees or more.
The fee values 50000 and 12345 paise are converted to rupees inline using the glossary's paise definition. No other numeric values appear.
Terms are clear and match the intent and glossary (front-desk staff, Inactive, Completed, Cancelled, No-show). The body matches the front matter.

findings.text: REQ-11 (rest of the page unchanged, including actions) is checked only for Scheduled and Cancelled appointments. Completed and No-show are separate partitions with different actions, and neither has an unchanged check.

cites.quote: Given a Scheduled appointment with history entries
The rest of the appointment page, including its `actions` and history, is unchanged.

findings.suggested_fix: Add S-3 ACs, or extend AC4/AC5, so that Completed and No-show appointments also show the same actions, history and other fields as before the change.

findings.text: Both fee ACs use fees under 1,000 rupees (₹500.00, ₹123.45). If the doctors list groups thousands, an appointment page that skips grouping still passes, which weakens the REQ-4 'same way as the doctors list' check.

cites.quote: then both show the fee as ₹123.45, with ₹ and two decimals
The fee is shown the same way as on the doctors list

findings.suggested_fix: Change S-1 AC4 to use a fee of 1,000 rupees or more (for example 150000 paise, which is 1500 rupees), compared against the doctors list.

findings.text: S-3 AC2 and AC3 only check what the page renders. A likely wrong implementation loads the whole doctor or patient record into the appointment response and hides fields in the UI; that would still pass.

cites.quote: then none of the doctor's contact details are shown
Medical history appears only on the `patient's own page`, never in lists, the dashboard or logs.

findings.suggested_fix: Have AC2 and AC3 also check that the data loaded for the appointment page has no doctor contact details and no patient medical history.

findings.text: S-3 bundles four separate constraints (doctor link, no contact details, no medical history, rest unchanged) into one story, so it does not deliver a single outcome.

cites.quote: The fee is shown the same way as on the doctors list: `₹` with two decimals.
Fees are stored and sent as integer paise.
Blood group, allergies, chronic conditions, current medications and notes of one patient.
A doctor, patient, department or specialization kept for history but not offered for new use.
